title: Cohomological bounds for a complete complex from residue Tor amplitude
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], meaning that every open cover has a finite subcover, with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_X$, the inverse limit of the constant quotient ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived complete for its quotient tower, meaning that the quotient maps exhibit $K$ as a derived limit of $(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(R/\varpi^n)_X)_{n\geq1}$, with its canonical reduction transitions and all terms viewed in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ by restriction of scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Suppose there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $K_1=K\otimes^L_{B_X}k_X$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: for every site object $V\to X$ and every sheaf $N$ of $k_V$-modules, $H^j((K_1|_V)\otimes^L_{k_V}N)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then $H^j(K)=0$ for every $j\notin[a,b]$. No constructibility or local constancy of the residue cohomology is required.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof of (1) and (2): these two arguments use completeness and finite residue Tor amplitude, not constructibility; Tag 099Q, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles, and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles. Transfer from constant to completed coefficients by algebraization.tex Tag 099I, lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence.

proof.text: Test the residue Tor interval at the identity pro-etale object and the coefficient unit sheaf. The identity pullback comparison and the tensor-unit identity on a K-flat representative give vanishing outside [a,b] for the actual residue derived scalar extension.

Unpack derived completeness: it already supplies one K-flat representative, its resolution, the canonical integral reduction tower, and a distinguished Roos triangle on its product with middle map 1-T. The resolution comparison and exact scalar restriction identify level zero with the residue reduction, so it has the same cohomology bounds.

Apply the successor triangle to each consecutive pair in this very tower. Induction in its cohomology long exact sequence proves that all reductions have cohomology in [a,b]. The following term H^(b+1)(F_0) vanishes, so the canonical transition on H^b is epi.

Pro-etale countable products are exact. The countable-AB4-star derived-category product theorem therefore says that each cohomology functor preserves these products. Apply cohomology directly to the Roos triangle supplied by completeness. Naturality of the product comparison identifies the image of 1-T with 1-T of the cohomology tower.

Outside [a,b], exactness forces vanishing except possibly in degree b+1: both adjacent cohomology products vanish otherwise. For degree b+1, top-degree transition maps are epi, so the pro-etale Milnor epimorphic theorem makes 1-T epi on their product. Exactness and vanishing of the other outer term force H^(b+1)(K)=0 as well. This proves precisely the original cohomology-vanishing conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09C2(1),(2), with sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0942 coefficient induction. The implementation applies cohomology to the actual Roos triangle already included in derived completeness, using exact pro-etale products; no separate Milnor cone or limit-uniqueness comparison is required.
